abstract.text: This article describes the KeyboardKit proxy engine and its utilities.

inlineContent.text: iOS keyboards use a
to integrate with the currently selected text field. The proxy lets you insert and delete text, get the currently selected text, move the input cursor, etc.

The native APIs are however very limited, which makes it hard to get detailed text information and to perform many standard operations. For instance, the native proxy can’t get all the text from the document, and lacks many other important capabilities.
KeyboardKit therefore extends the
with additional capabilities, like a document reader, and undo support. A
also has a custom
that can hijack the original proxy with a custom one.

with additional capabilities, such as the ability to get more content from the document, analyze words, sentences & quotations, end the current sentence, etc.

The native

doesn’t return all the text within the document. It instead cuts off the available text at any time, e.g. at the previous or next paragraph. This makes it hard to provide AI-based features that require more context.
KeyboardKit therefore has a
protocol that describes how to read a text document. KeyboardKit Pro extends
to implement this protocol, by reading the
The proxy also has
functions if you’re only interested in the text before or after the input cursor.

Text document read operations are best effort operations that makes the most of the limited native capabilities. It’s not guaranteed to return a correct result, and can struggle with complex text formats. You can customize the configuration to return better results.
The native
doesn’t support undoing changes, like typing, deleting and applying autocomplete suggestions. This makes it hard for users to undo unwanted changes.
KeyboardKit Pro therefore unlocks a
, which can be used to record and undo document changes. The
and
uses the same manager to handle changes.
The action handler will record any changes it makes while handling actions and autocomplete suggestions. You can tell it to undo changes with
action, or by calling the
function.

Subsequent changes of the same type will be recorded in smart chunks, to let us undo several changes with a single call. For instance, several subsequent character actions can be undone undo word by word. The same goes for deletions and autocompletions.

KeyboardKit lets users type, delete, and autocomplete freely and then use the undo manager to rollback change by change. Due to a keyboard extension’s limited control over the text document, moving the input cursor will reset the undo stack.
